settings.heading: How big should the face be?
settings.body:
Choose the face for the finger it will live on. Every listing gives the face in millimetres, so cut that size from paper, lay it on your finger and look in a mirror before you order.

  • Little finger: faces from 8 x 7mm to about 12 x 10mm sit neatly without catching on the next finger.
  • Ring or middle finger, or a statement little-finger ring: 13 x 11mm to 16 x 13mm, the traditional weight for a crest.
  • Horizontal faces sit across the finger and suit initials set in a line.
  • Face depth matters for engraving: each listing gives it, and only deeper faces take a seal.

settings.image_alt: A gold cushion signet ring engraved with the letter A, beside a pencil drawing of the same letter and an engraving tool
settings.heading: Engraved for you, priced before you order
settings.body:
Choose the engraving on the ring page and its price is added to your order there, so nothing is quoted later. Initials, a crest, a working seal or a few words inside the band: each type is set out below.

Want to see it first? Ask for a proof when you order.

settings.heading: Initials
settings.body: One, two or three letters on the face, in block capitals, serif, script or an interlaced monogram, or let us advise. £30 for one letter, £52.50 for two, £75 for three. Available on every signet.

settings.heading: Motif or crest
settings.body: Your family crest, an emblem or a symbol, in one of three styles. Classic, a clean cut outline: £120. Inverted, with the background cut away: £180. Layered, modelled in depth: £225. Send a photo or drawing after you order; if it needs redrawing first, we quote that before we start.

settings.heading: Seal engraving
settings.body: Cut deep and in reverse, so the ring presses a crisp, right-way-round impression into sealing wax, the signet's original purpose. £375. It needs a face at least 1.5mm deep, so it is offered on 35 of our 40 signets, and each listing says whether it is available.

settings.heading: Inside the band
settings.body: A name, a date or a few words, up to 35 characters, inside the shank, in Classic Script, Elegant Serif, Modern Sans or Block Capitals. £55, and it can be added to any face engraving.

settings.title: What is a signet ring?
settings.content: A signet ring has a flat face, traditionally engraved with a seal or symbol that identified its owner. Today it may be plain, engraved with initials or a crest, or set with a stone, and it is chosen as much for personal meaning, or simply for its shape, as for tradition.

settings.title: Can anyone wear a signet ring?
settings.content: Yes. Signet rings are not reserved for a gender, a family or a tradition. Choose the face size, band width and design around your hand and what you like, and wear it however feels right to you.

settings.title: Which finger is a signet ring worn on?
settings.content: In Britain the convention is the little finger of the left hand, a habit of the royal family since Queen Victoria's sons. Today it is worn on any finger, and sometimes as a wedding ring. Whichever you choose, measure that finger: a little finger is usually several sizes smaller than a ring finger. We post a free UK ring sizer.

settings.title: Which face shape and size should I choose?
settings.content: Oval is the classic and takes a crest or three initials comfortably. Cushion has softer corners and more room for detail. The shield is the heraldic shape, made for a crest. Round, square, hexagon and octagon faces feel more contemporary, and the heart suits a single initial. For size, cut the face from paper at the size the listing gives and try it on the finger it will be worn on.

settings.title: Cast or die-struck: what is the difference?
settings.content: A cast signet is made by pouring molten metal into a mould, which gives fine, crisp shapes. A die-struck signet is stamped from solid metal under great pressure, which makes the face denser so engraving stays sharp. Both are solid metal and hallmarked. Die-struck rings are also made in rose gold.

settings.title: What is the difference between engraving and seal engraving?
settings.content: Surface engraving reads correctly on the ring and suits initials and monograms. Seal engraving is cut deeper and in reverse, so that pressed into wax it prints the right way round. It needs a deep face, so it is offered on most of our signets, and each listing says whether it is available.

settings.title: How much does engraving cost?
settings.content: Initials cost £30 to £75 for one to three letters, a motif or crest £120 to £225 depending on style, and a seal engraving £375; engraving inside the band is £55. You choose it on the ring page and the price is shown before you order.

settings.title: Can you engrave our family crest?
settings.content: Yes. Send us a photograph, a drawing or an old signet, and we will prepare it for engraving; we can send you a proof first if you would like one. If your artwork needs redrawing first we quote that before starting. If you are unsure whether a crest is your family's, the College of Arms can advise.

settings.title: 9ct, 14ct, 18ct or platinum?
settings.content: 9ct gold, hallmarked 375, is the traditional signet metal: hard-wearing and paler in colour. 14ct, hallmarked 585, sits between the two. 18ct, hallmarked 750, has the richest colour but is softer, so it shows wear sooner. Platinum, hallmarked 950, is the heaviest and holds fine engraving well; it is offered on most designs.

settings.title: Can a signet ring be resized later?
settings.content: Usually. A plain or engraved signet is resized at the back of the shank without touching the face. Stone-set signets can be adjusted within a size or two with care. Every ring we make includes one free resize within 12 months of delivery, but getting the size right before engraving is always best.

settings.title: How long does a signet ring take?
settings.content: Every signet is made to order, and we confirm the making time before you order. An engraved crest adds about a week, and a seal engraving about two weeks.

  • Lifetime warranty against manufacturing defects.
